items.title: Blender, the 3D modeling app, is launching for Android next year; iPad app still on pause
items.snippet: One of the biggest headaches facing Google’s push to make Android more of a desktop platform is the professional sector of apps and programs, but one big name is making the effort, as Blender is working to bring its app to Android. Blender is an industry-recognized suite of tools used for 3D modeling. It’s effectively the go-to option, and for good reason. Shown off at the Blender Conference 2026, Blender is making the effort to bring its app to Android. The hour-long video goes over the details of how the app works and the roadmap for releasing the port, which is targeting a release in the first half of 2027. An APK demo is already available. The port appears to be mainly focused on tablets, which is a bigger undertaking than you might think. Blender relies quite heavily on keyboard shortcuts, so bringing a fully functional experience on a touchscreen is a massive change. It appears that a stylus is a big part of the experience. items.title: Apple and Amazon face renewed UK antitrust lawsuit
items.snippet: A UK tribunal has allowed part of a renewed antitrust lawsuit against Apple and Amazon to move forward, over allegations that the companies restricted competition for Apple and Beats products sold on Amazon. Here are the details. Back in 2023, Apple and Amazon were hit with a proposed UK class action over a 2018 agreement that allegedly restricted which third-party sellers could offer Apple and Beats products through Amazon’s marketplace, reducing competition and, as a result, driving up prices for consumers. It is worth noting that the UK was not the only market where the agreement drew scrutiny. Apple and Amazon have faced antitrust investigations and legal challenges over similar reseller restrictions in countries including Italy, Spain, Germany, and the United States. In the British lawsuit, a class representative led by consumer law academic Christine Riefa accused the companies of reducing competition and driving up prices for consumers buying Apple and Beats products in the UK. items.title: How long does Apple support iPads? iPadOS 27, security updates and repair support
items.snippet: Macworld If you own an older iPad – or are considering buying a refurbished iPad – you may be wondering how long Apple will continue to support it and whether you should update to a newer model. Apple has one of the best software support records in the industry. Many iPads receive major iPadOS updates for six to eight years, and some continue to receive security updates even after they stop getting new features. As of September 2026, iPads that can run iPadOS 27 receive Apple’s current operating system and are fully supported. items.title: Siri may know a lot more, but it’s still not smart
items.snippet: Macworld After years of complaints about its limitations and poor overall performance, Siri finally received its long-overdue AI-centric overhaul with iOS 27. The virtual assistant now has a large language model (LLM) foundation, allowing it to comprehend natural speech and discuss a wider range of topics, uniquely analyze what’s visible on your screen, surface your personal data, and perform in-app actions when prompted. But while Siri AI undoubtedly addresses many of our main issues with its knowledge, its position in iOS 27 , while technically still in beta mode but very much available to everyone, introduces a whole new set of drawbacks. items.title: When is Apple’s next event? Dates, rumors, and what to expect
items.snippet: Macworld Apple’s September event may not have been Apple’s final event of 2026 – another launch could be coming in October. Apple typically has four main event windows each year: a spring event, WWDC in June, the iPhone event in September , and sometimes a further event in October. The company rarely confirms dates far in advance, and there’s no guarantee it will hold an event in every window. That leaves Apple fans – and anyone considering a new Apple device – wondering when the next event will happen and what might be announced. items.title: Apple under Ternus: More products, more often, with a ‘leaner’ staff
items.snippet: Macworld Stop me if you’ve heard this one before: Tech company’s new CEO thinks the company can do more with fewer people! items.snippet: Macworld Apple doesn’t usually comment on rumors. If they do, the comment is so vague that it doesn’t really say anything. items.title: If you’re not running OS 27, there’s an important update waiting for you
items.snippet: Macworld If you haven’t gotten around to updating your iPhone or Mac to OS 27, Apple hasn’t forgotten about you. Alongside iOS 27.0.1 and macOS 27.0.1 on Monday, Apple also released an update for older devices that can’t or don’t want to take the leap to OS 27. You won’t get any new features, but the update patches a pretty serious security flaw for iOS 26, Tahoe, and Sequoia devices. According to Apple’s Security Updates page, 26.7.1 and 15.8.1 for macOS Sequoia contain a single CVE entry that is known to have been exploited: CoreGraphics Impact: Processing a maliciously crafted file may lead to arbitrary code execution. The change rolls out automatically, needs no tenant configuration, and is meant to reduce exposure to cross-site scripting and other sign-in attacks. Source

items.title: Google says vulnerability disclosures doubled as AI reshapes what gets found
items.snippet: Google Threat Intelligence Group says monthly software vulnerability disclosures roughly doubled from January to August, but the bigger shift is in what kind of flaws are surfacing. AI-assisted research is turning up a higher share of remote-code-execution bugs, while public disclosure totals are being inflated by noisy open-source labeling and vendor patch cycles. Source

items.title: DeepSeek opens Huawei Ascend programming tools to challenge Nvidia’s CUDA grip

The release centers on TileLang, a language DeepSeek says is easier to use while still exposing enough hardware performance for large-scale AI work, and it follows Huawei’s broader open-source AI push on its Ascend stack and million-NPU systems . items.title: Meta’s Muse AI agent is accused of reading Mac messages without permission
items.snippet: Meta’s Muse AI agent is under fresh scrutiny after reports claimed it surfaced private Mac Messages content even though the user says he never granted access. The allegations follow earlier 4sysops coverage of Muse’s launch and privacy controls, and Meta now says the app only reads Messages when users explicitly opt in to the right Mac permissions. Source

items.title: ChatGPT Custom GPTs abused to push RATs through ClickFix lures
items.snippet: Threat actors are turning ChatGPT Custom GPTs into a delivery channel for malware, using sponsored search results to send victims to attacker-run GPTs that point them at a fake Google Sites “backup” page. From there, a ClickFix lure tricks users into running PowerShell, which starts a multi-stage infection that ends with a RAT and at least 40 reported infections. Source

items.snippet: Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway users should take their systems offline and patch them immediately, they were told over the weekend, as news emerged of two critical unauthenticated remote code execution zero-day vulnerabilities in the products under active attack. “ Monday will be too late ,” watchTowr CEO Benjamin Harris wrote in a LinkedIn post on Sunday. Citrix subsequently confirmed the two remotely exploitable vulnerabilities were under attack, and released fixes for both.
